ptc_statement.text: a positive temperature coefficient (PTC) means power reduces as it gets hotter, reducing hazards in the event of a thermal runaway

power_graph.note: E3D's model curves: 40 W HeaterCore about 42 W at 0 degC, about 25 W at 300 degC

thermal_estimates.block_capacity_basis: 8 g brass nozzle x 0.38 J/gK + 9 g HeaterCore (alumina/bronze, about 0.4 J/gK); the cold end of the nozzle tube is not heated

hardware_over_temperature_cut_off.finding: No off-the-shelf hotend with a built-in one-shot cut-off, and no thermal fuse rated to sit on a 250-300 degC heater block, was found on a reachable host. The HeaterCore's PTC winding is the real product feature that limits a stuck-on heater: at 24 V it delivers 40 W at 23 degC and 24^2 / (14.4 x (1 + 0.002078 x (T - 23))) W at T: 27.2 W at 250 degC, 25.4 W at 300 degC, 21.2 W at 450 degC. It reduces fault power; it does not remove it.
options_not_verified: axial thermal cut-offs (SEFUSE SF-E class) stop at about 240 degC rated functioning temperature: recalled; they cannot sit on the block
a bimetal disc thermostat (KSD301 class, ceramic body, normally closed, 250-300 degC) is the usual hardware answer but is 16 mm across and has no seat on a Revo or V6 hot side: recalled
a thermal cut-off clamped to the heat sink (trips when the cold side overheats) with the PSU relay the design already has: indirect
